3.14.3.en: * This is what the prophet proclaims about the last judgment, in which the wicked will not be happy even in appearance, but will clearly be in utmost misery, while the righteous will not suffer any distress or misery, even temporary, but will enjoy complete, eternal happiness. He had previously quoted similar expressions about these men, when he said: "Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them" (Mal 2:17). I say this happens because of understanding the Law of Moses in a carnal way, therefore they murmured against God.

3.14.4.en: * Those who are spiritually immature place their trust more in temporal promises, and serve God looking to such rewards. For when the wicked prosper they are greatly troubled. Therefore Malachi continues, for their enlightenment, distinguishing between the eternal blessings of the New Testament, which the righteous alone receive, and the bare temporal blessings of the Old Testament, which the wicked often do not receive. He says: "Your words have been stout against me, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, What have we spoken so much against thee? Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts? And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up; yea, they that tempt God are even delivered" (Mal 3:13-15).

3.14.5.en: * "We call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up" (Mal 3:14-15). Such complaints drove the prophet to ask for the hastening of the last judgment, in which the wicked will be far from pretending to happiness, for their misery will be evident to all. The righteous, no longer troubled by passing sorrows, will enjoy a clear, infinite blessedness. Malachi gave a similar explanation to those who by their murmuring vex the Lord: "Every one that doeth evil (thinks) he is good in the sight of the LORD, and that He delighteth in such." The only point I wish to stress is that such murmurings against God are the fruit of the non-spiritual interpretation of the Law.

3.14.6.en: St. Augustine * I beg you to contemplate the virtue of the righteous man (Malachi) and the arrogance of the Jews. He who feels that there is no sin in him pronounces a very harsh sentence on himself when he says: "We have sinned, we have walked as rebels against the Law, we have done evil." But those who were filled with myriads of evils did the opposite when they said: "We have kept it, glorifying" (Mal 3:14-15) LXX. The righteous usually walk in meekness after practicing what is good, and the wicked in general glorify themselves after they sin... I say this so that we may avoid the sinner and imitate the righteous.

3.15.s.en: 6. His dealing with them as sons:

3.15.0.en: 16 Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name. 17 "And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him. 18 Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

3.15.1.en: Returning to God does not stop at giving to the brethren of the Lord, nor at the spiritual understanding of the concept of worship, but it befits the believers to realize the truth of God as a Father who has compassion on them as His children; thus they enjoy the spirit of discernment, so they distinguish the righteous who live the life of sonship to God, and the wicked who disobey the heavenly Father.

3.15.2.en: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name. [16]

3.15.3.en: Having presented the view of the worshipers of the Lord who worship in a literal, deadly way with corrupt conduct, so that they saw it as a source of sorrow, he now presents to us the view of those who fear the Lord and revere Him and think upon His name. Here he links godliness, or the fear of the Lord, with constant preoccupation with God. For those who bear the fear of the Lord as loving sons fear to wound their relationship with Him, so all their thoughts, feelings, senses, and emotions are absorbed in the Lord and in His name, sweet in their inner mouths.

3.15.4.en: Those who have this sweet spiritual experience will not cease to bear witness to the name of the Lord and His saving work. "And spake often one to another," for "out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh" (Mt 12:34). "A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things" (Mt 12:35).

3.15.5.en: The spiritual man speaks, not only with his lips and tongue, but by his conduct, his thoughts, and his features, bearing witness to the Kingdom of God dwelling in him.

3.15.6.en: How wonderful are his words: "And the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him," for He longs for the speech of those who love Him, His pious ones; He listens to them and hears the words of their hearts, and records as in a book of remembrance, esteeming every word they utter. The heavenly Bridegroom says to the human soul sanctified in Him: "Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes" (Song 4:9); "Let me hear thy voice, let me see thy countenance; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely" (Song 2:14).

3.15.7.en: "And a book of remembrance was written before him": this is a human expression that reveals to us in our language God's esteem for the words of His children and their holy thoughts, their tears and the sighs of their hearts. As the psalmist says: "Put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?" (Ps 56:8).

3.15.8.en: * He says this not as though there were a book on high and people writing, but by the book he means precious and precise knowledge, as he says: "The LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book...was written," and also "the books were opened" (Dan 7:10).

3.16.0.en: St. John Chrysostom And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him. [17]

3.16.1.en: God esteems not only the words of those who fear Him, their thoughts and feelings, but He esteems their persons, and ascribes them to Himself as His children: "They shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts." He counts them His own treasure, "when I make up my jewels" (lit. "I make His own"), so He calls Himself: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." He is the God of every person who counts God as his own, and so is God's own. Whoever esteems God and glorifies Him, God esteems him and pours the splendor of His glory into his depths.

3.16.2.en: As the Lord Himself says: "And will be the glory in the midst of her" (Zech 2:5). "As the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee" (Isa 62:5). "Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God" (Isa 62:3).

3.17.0.en: Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not. [18]

3.17.1.en: Since the Lord accepts from those who fear Him the least services and esteems them because they come from His own, from His children beloved to Him, He gives the finest gift, which is the knowledge that flows from Him. He gives them the spirit of discernment, so that by His Spirit they distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, and between him that serveth God and him that serveth Him not, a matter which belongs to God, the Knower of hearts.

3.17.2.en: * Now the proud are called happy; yes, those who tempt God are delivered. But the Lord afterward threatens them with the day of judgment, and announces beforehand the distinction that will take place between the righteous and the wicked, saying to them thus: "Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not" (Mal 3:18).

3.17.4.en: Purify my depths and dwell in them, O Holy One!

3.17.5.en: * You sent St. John the Baptist as Your messenger, to prepare the way before You by proclaiming repentance!

3.17.6.en: You gave me Your Holy Spirit, who grants me adoption.

3.17.7.en: In the waters of Baptism You raised me to the bosom of Your Father, and presented me as a son who bears Your marvelous righteousness!

3.17.8.en: What shall I render to You before this surpassing love?

3.17.9.en: * Dwell, O Lord, in my depths, O consuming Fire, burning up all the thorns that choke my soul, and make of me a fiery being, whom all the waters of the world cannot quench.

3.17.10.en: Sanctify me, purify me, that I may become an icon of You, O You who alone are Holy!

3.17.11.en: * I see You coming down to my weakness; I long to return to You, O true Love!

3.17.12.en: You come to me through the suffering, the sick, and the needy, for You are the Father of the fatherless, the Judge of the widows, and the Shepherd of straying souls, to bring them back to Your marvelous pastures!

3.17.13.en: * Grant me also to worship You as You desire.

3.17.14.en: I worship You in spirit and in truth, that I may rise above the letter, and enjoy the Spirit!

3.17.15.en: Grant me the wings of the Spirit, that I may fly to You, rise above all earthly things, and ask nothing of the temporal.

3.17.16.en: * Finally grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may know that You are my Father.

3.17.17.en: I see even in Your chastenings a fatherhood, tenderness, and heavenly care.

3.17.18.en: I distinguish righteousness from evil, and I am in touch with Your righteous saints, and I do not take part with the wicked deceivers.

4.0.0.en: 1 "For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.

4.0.1.en: In the previous chapter he spoke of the spirit of discernment by which we realize that God is our Father, for He has compassion on us as His children, and sent His Word incarnate to unite us to Himself by our return through the work of His grace. But it is also fitting to realize that He is the Holy One who does not appease sin, but burns it as in an oven (furnace). He came to stretch out His hands in love to all humanity, but if a man insists on the pride of his heart and does evil, he casts himself under eternal judgment and perishes.

4.0.2.en: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch. [1]

4.0.3.en: The prophet Malachi prophesies about the day of the coming of the incarnate Word to accomplish salvation, for although He stretches out His arms to all humanity, He came to send fire. Whoever believes in Him enjoys eternal life, but he who exalts himself against Him and rejects Him burns like stubble in the midst of the fire. This is what the psalmist prophesied about the Messiah: "Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the LORD shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them" (Ps 21:9).

4.0.4.en: God, who knows the hearts, alone is able to separate the stubble from the gold, the proud from the humble. The former are counted workers of evil who burn in the fire, so that He leaves them neither root nor branch, and the latter increase in splendor and purity.

4.0.5.en: Some had previously called the proud blessed because they are happy in this world (Mal 3:15); now their reality appears, that they are stubble burning in the oven, becoming ashes.

4.0.6.en: Perhaps by the proud here he means those like the company of the Pharisees, who were exalting themselves by their knowledge and their literal righteousness, and resisted the Lord Christ, and in their resistance became like stubble that cannot endure the flame of fire. As for the workers of evil, he means by them the rest of the Jews who rejected the Savior.

4.0.7.en: The Lord left them neither root nor branch, for He allowed Titus afterward to destroy Jerusalem and utterly annihilate the Temple. This is fulfilled in perfect form on the day of the last coming of the Lord Christ to judge the wicked and reward the true believers, those who fear the Lord and revere Him.

4.0.8.en: * But when the day of divine vengeance for innocent blood comes, the Holy Spirit announces this by the prophet Malachi: "Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, that shall burn as an oven..." (Mal 4:1).

4.0.9.en: St. Cyprian * The whole earth will be like lead melting in the fire; then the hidden and open works of men will be revealed.

4.0.10.en: The so-called Clement of Rome * His two comings: one in truth in which He became man subject to scourgings... and the second in which He will come on the clouds (Dan 7:13), where He comes on the day on which He burns like a fire (Mal 4:1), and smites the earth with the sword of His mouth (Isa 11:4), and slays the wicked with the breath of His lips, and with Him is a fan in His hands, and He purges His floor, and gathers the wheat into His garner in truth, and burns up the chaff with unquenchable fire (Mt 3:12; Lk 4:17).

4.0.11.en: St. Irenaeus * The Lord foretells that the transgressors will be burned and perish, for they are strangers to the divine race, defilers of holy things, those who have not been born again spiritually and become children of God. For these alone can escape: those who have been born again and marked with the sign of Christ. God says in another place, when sending His angels for the destruction of the world and the death of the human race, threatening with the greatest terror in the last time: "Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity: Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark" (Ezek 9:5). Moreover: what is this mark, and in what part of the body is its place...? God made this clear in another place, saying: "Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof" (Ezek 9:4). And that the sign belongs to the passion of Christ and His blood, and that everyone in whom this sign is found is kept in safety and no harm befalls him, is also confirmed by God's testimony: "And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt" (Ex 12:13). What happened previously in a type by the slaying of the lamb was fulfilled in Christ, the Truth who came afterward, and just as when Egypt was smitten it was not possible for the Jews to escape except by the blood of the lamb and its sign, so when the world begins to be destroyed and smitten, only he in whom the blood of Christ and His sign are found escapes (Ezek 9:4; Rev 7:3; 9:4).

4.1.s.en: 2. The rising of the Sun of righteousness:

4.1.0.en: 2 "But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.

4.1.1.en: Lest anyone fall into despair because of his sins, the Lord announces His coming as the Sun of righteousness, rising upon souls and dispelling their darkness, but not by compulsion against their will. He is the divine heavenly Physician who comes down to His sick, and heals them if they accept His work in them.

4.1.2.en: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.

4.1.3.en: And ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall. [2]

4.1.4.en: Just as the Lord Christ came to send fire that purifies those who believe in Him, and burns the deniers who persist in their denial to the last breath, so He is a light to every man who receives Him, and he is counted one who fears the Lord and reveres Him. He rose upon the world in His first coming as with two wings to heal every sick soul, and He will rise with the light of His splendor in His second coming to give those who fear Him fellowship in eternal glories. That day will be a day of darkness and gloom to those who reject Him, and a day of joyful wedding and unceasing light to those who believed in Him and enjoyed the new life in Him.

4.1.5.en: "Ye shall go forth": as the sick enjoy the Sun of righteousness and receive healing, they go forth as to their work. Instead of lying long in incapacity to work for the Kingdom of God, they go forth to bear witness and to build up souls in the Lord the Savior.

4.1.6.en: "Grow up" or "increase," as health returns to them, so they move forward advancing in grace, knowledge, and divine wisdom, that perhaps they may attain to the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ, to "a perfect man" (Eph 4:13).

4.1.7.en: Here he likens them to "calves of the stall," or calves of the manger, which quickly grow and become strong and useful to their owners. Some see that the man who enjoys the light of the Sun of righteousness goes forth as to the field like the stall-fed calf that leaps in the open air in merriment, jumping for joy.

4.1.8.en: St. Hippolytus sees that the Lord Christ, the Sun of righteousness, does not leave His Church in the days of the great tribulation, in the time of the Antichrist, but rises upon her with His light... [He who stretches out His hands on the holy wood spreads His wings, right and left, and calls to Himself all who believe in Him, and covers them as a hen does her chicks. So He says by the mouth of Malachi: "But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings" (Mal 4:2)].

4.1.9.en: * Behold, your Savior has now come to save you, and Christ the Sun of righteousness has arisen to you to enlighten you.

4.1.10.en: The Acts of Philip * The moon is understood symbolically as the Church, because she has no light of her own, but is enlightened by the only-begotten Son of God, who is mentioned in many places in the Holy Bible symbolically as the Sun (Mal 4:2, etc.).

4.1.11.en: * When shall the horn of His people be exalted? When the Lord comes, and our sun rises, not the sun that is seen with the eye, which rises on the good and the evil (Mt 5:45), but that of which it is said: to you who hear God "shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings" (Mal 4:2). This is the one about which the proud and the wicked say afterward: "The light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us" (Wis 5:6).

4.1.12.en: St. Augustine * (Mary) is the eastern gate of which the prophet Ezekiel spoke, that it is always shut and always shining, and is sealed or revealed to the Holy of Holies; through her entered and went out the "Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2), the high priest after the order of Melchizedek (Heb 5:10).

4.1.13.en: St. Jerome * If the blind man suffers from not seeing the material sun, what deprivation befalls the sinner who does not enjoy the true light?

4.1.14.en: St. Basil the Great * He gives His servants a share in His name, for as He is the Light, He calls His saints light, saying: "Ye are the light of the world" (Mt 5:14), and He calls His servants by that which He is, the "Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2): "Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun" (Mt 13:43).

4.1.15.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus * Our ship was not made of wooden planks, but was formed and quickly assembled by the Holy Scripture. The stars in heaven do not guide us on our journey, but the Sun of righteousness guides our ship on its way. For as we sit by the tiller we do not wait for the breezes of the wind, but we look for the gentle breeze of the Spirit.

4.1.16.en: St. John Chrysostom * Do not place your trust in the sun without reflection, for it is truly the eye of the world, the delight of the day, the beauty of the heavens, the charm of nature, the splendor of creation. When you look at it, contemplate its Maker. When you marvel at it, glorify its Creator. If the sun, as a companion of nature and a sharer in it, is so delightful, how great is the goodness that is in the Sun of righteousness? If the sun is so swift, and by its swift course by day and night is able to pass through all things, how much greater is He who fills all things continually and everywhere?

4.1.17.en: St. Ambrose * From the East atonement came to you, for from there came a man called "the East," who became mediator between God and mankind; therefore you are called by this to look always toward the East, where the Sun of righteousness rises upon you, where the light is born for you, so that you may no longer walk in darkness, and that darkness may not overtake you on the last day. Therefore the night of the fog of ignorance will not fall upon you, but you will be found always in the light of knowledge, and you will have always the day of faith, and you will keep always the light of love and peace.

4.1.18.en: * When He is transfigured His face shines as the sun, that He may be revealed to the children of light who put off the works of darkness and put on the armor of the children of light (Jn 12:36; Rom 13:12-13), and are no longer children of darkness nor children of the night, but children of the day and walk honestly as in the day (Rom 13:13; 1 Thess 5:5). So when He reveals Himself, He shines upon them not as the ordinary sun but as the Sun of righteousness.

4.1.19.en: * There was no night in Peter when he confessed: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Mt 16:16), when the heavenly Father revealed this to him. But there was night in him at the moment of his denial (Mt 26:74-75). And in the present example, when Judas received the sop he went out immediately (Jn 13:30), because the One who is called "the East" was not present with him, for he left the Sun of righteousness behind when he went out. And Judas, who was filled with darkness, pursued Jesus, but the darkness he had acquired did not comprehend the Light he pursued. For this reason also when he spoke a word of justification: "I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood" (Mt 27:4), "went and hanged himself" (Mt 27:5); for Satan who was in him led him to evil and strangled him, since Satan touched his very soul at that time. For the Lord was not able to say to Satan in his favor what He said in Job's favor: "But save his life" (Job 1:12; 2:6).

4.1.20.en: Origen the Scholar * When man transgressed the commandment, Satan cast a dark veil over the soul. And when grace comes it removes the veil completely, so that when the soul becomes pure and regains its original nature, and is considered clear and without blemish, it waits always in clarity, with its pure eye, for the glory of the true Light and the true Sun of righteousness shining with its rays within the heart itself.

4.1.21.en: * Not only until the day when the last Adam came, but even to this day, those on whom the "Sun of righteousness," that is Christ, has not risen, and whose soul's eyes have not been opened and enlightened by the true Light, are still under the same darkness of sin, and under the same influence of the passions, and are under the very same punishment, since they have not yet eyes with which to see the Father.

4.1.22.en: St. Macarius the Great * He is the Sun of righteousness, revealed from heaven, surrounded by His visible nature, and returning to Himself.

4.1.23.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * As we know that Christ is the true Light (Jn 1:9) who is not approached by falsehood, we learn from this the necessity of enlightening our life by the true Light. But the virtues are the rays of the Sun of righteousness streaming for our enlightenment, through which we cast off the works of darkness (Rom 13:12) that we may walk honestly as in the day (Rom 13:13) and renounce the hidden things of shame (2 Cor 4:2). As we do everything in the light we become the light itself, shining on others (Mt 5:15-16), the light that has its own character.

4.1.24.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * But when the only-begotten Son of God Himself called us to this sonship, He called us to be like Him, therefore He said: "For he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust." But what is this sun?! It is either a sun invisible to the bodily eye, that is, that Wisdom of which it was said that it is "the brightness of the everlasting light" (Wis 7:26), as it was said of it, "the Sun of righteousness shines upon me," and also: "Unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise" (Mal 4:2).

4.1.25.en: Likewise the rain would be invisible, meaning by it the teachings of the truth and their watering of our souls, because the Lord Christ came for the good and the evil, and was preached to the just and the unjust.

4.1.26.en: * Or it is that visible sun which all creatures see, and likewise the rain is that visible rain by which the plants grow that nourish the body. And this interpretation I think more probable, because the spiritual sun rises only on the good and the holy, for we see in the book of Wisdom the wicked weeping and saying: "The sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:6), and the spiritual rain waters only the good, because by the wicked one he meant that vineyard of which it was said: "I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it" (Isa 5:6).

4.1.27.en: * "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 4:26), and yet the sun has set many times. Leave your wrath also, since we now celebrate the days of the great Sun, this Sun of which the Holy Scripture says "unto you... shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings" (Mal 4:2). What does he mean by "in his wings"? That is, in His protection, for it is said in the Psalms: "Hide me under the shadow of thy wings" (Ps 17:8). As for those who repent on the day of judgment, but after the time has passed, and who will grieve but without profit, the book of Wisdom has prophesied beforehand what they will say when they repent and groan for anguish of spirit: "What hath pride profited us? or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow... we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:6, 8, 9). That Sun rises on the righteous only, but as for this sun that we see daily, God maketh His sun to rise on the evil and on the good" (Mt 5:45). The righteous ask to see that Sun, and it dwells in our hearts by faith. So if you are angry, do not let this Sun go down in your hearts upon your wrath, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath." Lest you be angry, and the Sun of righteousness set from you, and you remain in darkness.

4.1.28.en: St. Augustine * This applies to the first coming of our Savior and the second coming: He rose in His first coming like a kind of sun for us who sit in darkness and shadows, and frees us from sin, and gives us fellowship in righteousness, and covers us with spiritual gifts as wings, and gives healing to our souls. And in His second coming, to those who have labored in the present life, He appears either in accordance with their will or against it; and as a just Judge He judges with justice and gives the promised good things. Just as the material sun in rising awakens those whom sleep has seized to rise for work, so in His coming He raises those in the grip of the long sleep of death.

4.1.29.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus * Since God is a spiritual light (1 Jn 1:5), and Christ is called in the Holy Scriptures the Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2), and the breaking of the morning (the dawn), the East is the direction that must be appointed for His worship.

4.2.s.en: 3. The Sun of righteousness, giver of victory:

4.2.0.en: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts. [3]

4.2.1.en: The secret of their joy and merriment is their enjoyment of victory over the enemy of good and his wicked angels, who become ashes under their feet. They join the triumphal procession under the leadership of Christ the Head, who says: "Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (Jn 16:33). They fulfill the promise: "Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings" (Josh 10:4).

4.2.2.en: * We trust in Him who said: "Rejoice, I have overcome the world" (Jn 16:33), because we gain victory over our enemy the devil, by His help and protection.

4.2.3.en: * Why does He say to us: "Rejoice," except because He has overcome for us, and fought for us?

4.2.4.en: For where did He fight? He fought by taking our nature to Himself...

4.2.5.en: He overcame for us, to whom He showed His resurrection...

4.2.6.en: Cleave, O man, to God, who created you a man. Cleave to Him greatly, place your trust in Him.

4.2.7.en: Call upon Him, let Him be your strength. Say to Him: "In Thee, O Lord, is my strength."

4.2.8.en: Then you will sing when men threaten you, and what you sing the Lord Himself tells you: "In God I have put my trust: I will not be afraid what man can do unto me" (Ps 56:11).

4.2.9.en: St. Augustine * He permits us also to overcome, looking to the Author of our faith, and walking in the same way that He traveled for us... that we are not mortal because of our struggle with death, but immortal because of our victory... Does death corrupt our bodies? What is this? They will not remain in corruption, but will come to a better state...

4.2.10.en: Then let us overcome the world, let us run toward immortality, let us follow the King, let us set up the memorial of victory, let us despise the pleasures of the world. We do not need toil to accomplish this.

4.2.11.en: Let us turn our souls to heaven, and the whole world will flee! When you do not desire it you overcome it; if you mock it, it is conquered.

4.2.12.en: We are strangers and wanderers; may we not grieve over any grievous things of it.

4.3.s.en: 4. A new vision of the Law:

4.3.0.en: 4 "Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.

4.3.1.en: The Jews thought they were keeping the Law of Moses by offering many blemished offerings and sacrifices. Now He demands of them to remember the Law on the spiritual level, that they themselves may be without blemish, and God may accept their offerings.

4.3.2.en: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel.

4.3.4.en: The following statements (4-6) are a conclusion not to the book of Malachi alone but to the whole Old Testament. This conclusion came to prepare the people to await the coming of the Lord Christ, by examining the Law that bears witness to the Lord Christ, or the Law that leads us to Him, and as St. Peter says: "We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost" (2 Pet 1:19-21).

4.3.5.en: * The aim of the prophet is that the readers learn to give a spiritual interpretation of the Law, and find in it Christ the Judge, who distinguishes the righteous from the wicked. For it was not without reason that Christ said to the Jews: "For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me" (Jn 5:46). In truth, because of their merely literal interpretation of the Law and their inability to realize that its temporal promises are only symbols of the eternal rewards, they fell into a resentment that bore rebellion, so they said: "It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance..." (Mal 3:14-15).

4.3.6.en: St. Augustine * This Law is so holy and good that our Savior at a certain time, when He healed a leper, and healed afterward nine lepers, said to the first: "Go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them" (Mt 8:4; Mk 1:44). For He did not abolish the Law in any place.

4.3.7.en: The Didascalia * The first sign of obedience that you receive is the acceptance of the coming of Christ the Lord, who came for the salvation of all the people. He brings the Law to its goal and makes clear His way to perfection. Therefore it is good for you to believe in Him at His appearing and to know that He is the one of whom Moses and the prophets prophesied, that He fulfills the goal of the Law and proclaims the salvation of all in general.

4.4.s.en: 5. The coming of Elijah the prophet:

4.4.0.en: 5 "Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD: 6 And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse."

4.4.1.en: The Lord sent His messenger, St. John the Baptist, before His first coming to bring salvation. St. John the Baptist came in the fiery spirit of Elijah, and Elijah will be sent with Enoch in the days of the Antichrist to prepare the way for His last coming.

4.4.2.en: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD [5]

4.4.3.en: He demanded of them to return to the Law and to examine the Scripture, for the mission of the prophets ceases until the coming of him who has the spirit and zeal of Elijah to prepare the way for the coming of the Lord (Lk 1:17).

4.4.4.en: The Jewish interpreters were divided into two groups in their interpretation of this statement: one group thought that Elijah himself comes into the world to prepare the way for the Messiah. Others reckoned that a man comes in the spirit of Elijah.

4.5.s.en: Did Elijah the prophet come again?

4.5.0.en: When St. John the Baptist was asked whether he was Elijah he answered in the negative (Jn 1:22), while the Lord Christ said: "Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them" (Mt 17:12), "Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist" (Mt 17:13). St. Augustine explains that he had to come before the first coming of the Lord Christ and also the second. In the first coming Elijah did not come in his person, but St. John the Baptist bore his mind and his way of life, therefore the Lord Christ said of him that he is Elijah who was to come (Mt 11:14), but he did not come in his person, therefore John the Baptist said that he is not Elijah. But at the second and last coming of the Lord Christ Elijah will precede Him, coming in his own person and bearing witness against the Antichrist and being martyred.

4.5.1.en: * Since the Savior is the beginning of the resurrection of all the people, it was fitting that the Lord alone should rise from the dead, by whom also judgment enters the whole world, so that the worthy strivers may rely by him on the famous Mediator, for He Himself completed the way and was received into the heavens, and sat at the right hand of God the Father, and will be revealed again at the end of the world as the Judge. He is appointed for a certain role, and his forerunner must appear first, as was said by Malachi and the angel: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just, lest I come and smite the earth utterly" (cf. Mal 4:5-6). So he will come and announce the appearing of Christ from heaven. And signs and wonders will occur, so that men will be ashamed and return to repentance from their great evil.

4.5.2.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome * What is the source of your belief that Elijah who is to come will baptize? For he did not baptize the wood on the altar in the days of Ahab, when he needed a bath of water so that it would burn when the Lord appeared in fire (1 Kgs 18:21-38). He commanded the priests to do this, not once, but says: "Do it the second time. And they did it the second time" and also: "Do it the third time. And they did it the third time" (1 Kgs 18:34). So how will he who did not baptize at that time but gave to others that they should baptize, baptize when he comes at the completion of the things of which Malachi speaks?

4.5.3.en: Origen the Scholar * "And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God." He speaks of Elijah the prophet, who is the forerunner in the days of the Antichrist, to correct the churches and establish them in the face of the great, excessive persecution. We read that these things are foretold at the beginning of the Old Testament and the New Testament; for Malachi says: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the Tishbite, to turn the heart of the fathers to the children, according to the time of the suit, to turn the Jews to the faith of the people who succeeded him.

4.5.4.en: Victorinus, Bishop of Petovium * As the end of the times draws near, a great prophet will be sent to turn men to the knowledge of God, and he will receive power to work wonders. And when men do not listen to him he will shut up heaven and make it withhold its rain, and will turn their water into blood, and torment them with thirst and hunger. And if anyone seeks to harm him fire will go out of his mouth and burn him up.

4.5.5.en: Lactantius * It is inevitable that the two heralds (forerunners) of His coming must appear first, as was said by Malachi and the angel (the annunciation of Zacharias the priest of the birth of John the forerunner)... They (Elijah and Enoch) will come and announce the appearing of Christ, that He will be from heaven, and will work signs and bring back to repentance those who were overcome by evil and ungodliness.

4.5.6.en: St. Hippolytus And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers.

4.6.0.en: Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse. [6]

4.6.1.en: Father Victorinus sees in this statement an indication that a large number of the Jews will accept faith in the Lord Christ through the witness of Elijah the prophet in the last times at the coming of the Antichrist.

4.6.2.en: Shine with Your light in my depths

4.6.3.en: * You came to our world to dispel all darkness, You shine in every soul and raise it up as a luminous star.

4.6.4.en: You transform our darkness into light, and our shame into glory.

4.6.5.en: * Whoever rejects Your light loses his insight, and the darkness of ignorance settles on his mind, and the day of Your second coming becomes for him a terror.

4.6.6.en: * Enter, O Sun of righteousness, into my depths, and establish Your kingdom within me, that I may become gold refined by fire, and there be no place in me for dross.

4.6.7.en: * O heavenly Physician, take away my sickness, and grant me eternal healing.

4.6.8.en: Turn my life into unceasing jubilation.

4.6.9.en: Let me leap for joy among the heavenly ones.

4.6.10.en: * May I enjoy Your victory and triumph, so that the devil has no place within me, but by Your grace to me he becomes under my feet.

4.6.11.en: He has no more authority over me!

4.6.12.en: * I am waiting for You, O Giver of glory.

4.6.13.en: Send Elijah and Enoch to break the power of the Antichrist, and prepare the whole world to enjoy Your salvation.

4.6.14.en: My depths cry out to You:
